FT-002.adaptation: Accepted FT-002 rev 8: broader pinned corpus, repeated burst-edit and recovery performance gates, preserved source and capability identity, and byte/pixel parity published separately from compiler latency. Rev 7 just removed a parser quadratic that made a 500KB one-word edit 420ms; burst editing is the natural next risk because it is what real typing looks like and it is where reuse state could degrade across many consecutive edits rather than one. Note that open issue #21 remains unaddressed and is mine: a valid 500KB project emits 10.1MB in one reply and exceeds the 8 MiB runtime frame.

next_action: Propose compact or chunked transport to the Commander with measured byte breakdown; key names alone are 71 percent of a large reply.

origin/main.adaptation: Measured the byte breakdown before proposing anything: repeated key names account for about 71 percent of a large reply and payload data only 29 percent, so the durable fix is a compact or chunked transport, which is a contract decision the Commander owns. Bounding with an explicit diagnostic is the part that is mine and it turns a confusing malformed-frame rejection into an accurate statement of what happened.

summary: Issue #21 fixed: a valid 500KB project produced a 13.4MB reply that the runtime rejected as malformed. The reply is now bounded to the 8 MiB transport frame and says explicitly how many pages were not delivered and why. 15 suites pass.

usage.evidence: Reproduced: 516193 byte input produced 13381254 byte reply, 88902 items at 150.5 bytes each, exceeding the 8388608 byte frame. After the fix the same input produces 8303434 bytes, 157 of 253 pages, with an explicit error diagnostic naming the 96 undelivered pages. Regression test added.
